name: Multi-rate energy meter
summary: Energy meter that switches between registers by time or tariff signal so energy is billed at different rates.
description: A multi-rate meter has two or more registers and switches between them according to an internal clock or an external tariff signal. Older installations use a ripple control receiver or time switch to change rate, which is why the schematic may show a control input to the meter.

The symbol marks the multiple registers but not the rate schedule. Tariff periods are set by the supply agreement and meter programming, and the drawing should reference the tariff source rather than assume it from the meter form.
readingNotes: Look for an external tariff switching input.
Check that the register count matches the tariff.
distinction: A multi-rate meter splits energy by time or tariff; a bidirectional meter splits energy by direction.
